claims.explanation: Desoxycortone is a mineralocorticoid receptor (NR3C2) agonist, and its selective killing pattern tracks with NR3C2/NR3C1 expression and downstream corticosteroid-responsive signaling rather than any single lineage. The most sensitive lines are enriched for TP53 pathway loss combined with RAS/MAPK or PI3K pathway activation, which may cooperate with mineralocorticoid receptor-driven transcriptional programs to induce lethal stress, while lines with intact ARID1A/SMARCA4 chromatin-remodeling or PIK3CA/PTEN alterations tend to be protected. The virtual-cell signature (STAT3, NFATC3, CHEK1 up; CDC20, CCNB2 down) supports a mechanism involving cell-cycle arrest and stress-response signaling downstream of steroid receptor activation.

features.basis: mineralocorticoid receptor is the annotated primary target of desoxycortone
glucocorticoid receptor cross-reactivity of desoxycortone and steroid transport effects
TP53 mutation is near-universal in the most-killed lines and absent in several protected lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines are among the most sensitive
KRAS-mutant lung, colorectal, pancreatic, and soft-tissue lines are enriched in the sensitive group
ARID1A-mutant lines are enriched among the least-affected lines
PIK3CA-mutant lines appear predominantly in the protected group
PTEN-mutant breast, thyroid, and kidney lines are among the least affected
SMARCA4-mutant COV434 is among the most sensitive lines
virtual-cell L1000 signature shows STAT3 upregulation after desoxycortone
virtual-cell signature shows CHEK1 upregulation, suggesting replication-stress response
virtual-cell signature shows CDC20 downregulation, consistent with mitotic arrest in sensitive cells
